To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

NMR and pattern recognition methods were used to establish the CSF metabolic profiles of neuroinflammation in EAE rats and that the profiles of neuroinflamed CSF were different from healthy and peripheral inflamed CSF.
we were able to identify disease-specific markers in the CSF of rats with neuroinflammation (EAE model), which may help to develop an early diagnosis for MScl in humans.

we developed a novel method to detect neuroinflammation in the EAE model, which is a commonly accepted model for neuroinflammatory aspects of MScl, using a combination of advanced (NMR) spectroscopy and pattern analysis methods.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a diagnostic method for early stage MScl, using a novel approach, which combines (1)H-NMR spectroscopy, pattern recognition and multivariate statistics, and which may be used in the future as a molecular diagnostic tool.
the discovery of disease-specific markers for neuroinflammations in CSF using NMR spectroscopy.
the development of a novel approach for the diagnosis and monitoring of the early stages of MScl.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CSF profile of EAE-animals is distinct from healthy controls and peripheral inflammation and is characterized by a decrease in creatine, arginyl and lysyl metabolites.
the CSF metabolite profile of neuroinflammation differs from the CSF metabolites of peripheral inflammation, and is therefore suitable for early detection of neuroinflammations.
NMR spectroscopy is able to detect early stages of neuroinflammation in a reliable manner and that this is an important step in the development of a diagnostic tool for the early stage of MScl.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NMR and pattern recognition methods are able to distinguish neuroinflammations from healthy and peripherally inflammation, which may be useful for molecular diagnosis of neuroinflammations in humans.
we have developed and validated an NMR-based method that can distinguish neuroinflammatory disease from healthy and peripherally inflammatory conditions.
we can use the CSF metabolite pattern to distinguish between neuroinflammation (EAE), peripheral inflammation (peritoneal infection) and healthy animals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
NMR spectroscopy is a valuable method for the early detection of neuroinflammation in CSF.
NMR spectroscopy can detect early stage neurodegeneration and that the metabolic profile for early stage neurodegenerative diseases is distinct from other diseases.

the combination of advanced NMR spectroscopy with pattern recognition methods can be used to detect specific disease markers for neuroinflammations in the EAE model, and these markers are predictive for early neuroinflammatory disease in a second independent animal cohort.
